blocks.value: Average True Range (ATR) measures how much a stock typically moves during a trading period. It measures volatility, not direction.
Imagine This: Some beaches have calm waves while others have huge crashing waves. ATR measures the size of the waves, not whether they move left or right.
A higher ATR means the stock usually experiences larger price movements. A lower ATR indicates more stable price movements.
If Stock A usually moves ₹2 per day and Stock B usually moves ₹40 per day, Stock B has a much higher ATR.
Many traders use ATR while deciding Stop Loss levels.
